title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6559 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: US October PCE core inflation +0.3% m/m vs +0.3% expected

Prior month +0.2% Personal spending +0.3% vs +0.4% expected. Prior month +0.5% Real personal spending +0.0% vs 0.0% prior There are no big surprises here, though the market could have done without the slightly hot core year-over-year number. Last month I said we'd need another month to see if inflation was broadening. October doesn't settle that, but it doesn't make the worry go away either. Back-to-back core readings of 0.3% and 0.3% aren't consistent with getting anywhere near 2%. The more interesting part of the report is the consumer. Income beat by a wide margin, but spending fell short and real spending was flat for a second straight month. BEA says government benefits were boosted by one-time Medicare Improvement Fund premium rebates so that's likely the story. Most indications from retailers in reports from the past two weeks suggest that the US consumer is fine, in any case. Digging into the data core goods inflation was about +0.4% m/m in October, the hottest since February (+0.7%). It was +0.2% in September and around 0.1% in the summer.

title: US GDP 2nd Estimate for the 3rd quarter 4.3% vs 3.5 estimate

GDP deflator: 1.8% vs 2.3% expected. Previously 2.2%. Core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) prices: 2.5% vs 2.5% expected. Previously 2.5%. The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported 3.4% in its advance estimate, making this a 0.9 percentage point upward revision. U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) Household spending was stronger than first reported, with growth revised up to 4.2% from 3.8%. The inflation figures were more subdued. The GDP deflator came in below expectations at 1.8%, while core PCE inflation held at 2.5%, in line with forecasts. What drove the upward revision to Q3 GDP? US real GDP growth was revised up to 4.3% annualized from 3.4% in the advance estimate. Investment accounted for the largest upward revision, followed by consumer spending. Government spending added a little more, while exports and imports were slightly smaller drags. The chart shows the following contributions to annualized GDP growth, in approximate percentage points: Investment: +3.7 vs +3.3 in the advance estimate, the largest upward revision among the components. title: US October durable goods orders +0.2% vs +0.6% expected
body: Prior was 1.9% Ex-transport +0.5% vs +0.5% expected Prior ex-transport +0.5% Ex-defense +0.4% vs +2.3% prior Non-defense capital goods orders ex-air +1.2% vs +0.7% expected Prior +0.6% US durable goods orders continued to expand in October, giving another positive signal for the manufacturing sector. New orders for manufactured durable goods increased by $0.8 billion, or 0.2%, to $346.7 billion, following September's stronger 2.0% increase. The headline increase was relatively modest, but the underlying details were more encouraging. Excluding transportation, new orders rose 0.5%, while orders excluding defense increased 0.4%. This suggests that the expansion was not solely driven by volatile transportation or defence-related demand. Machinery was the main contributor to the monthly increase, with orders rising by $0.8 billion, or 1.8%, to $46.8 billion. The category has now increased in 21 of the past 22 months, highlighting the persistence of demand for industrial equipment and machinery. Overall, durable goods orders have increased in seven of the past eight months, showing that demand for long-lasting manufactured products remains relatively resilient. Keep in mind that the Durable Goods Orders report is almost never a market-moving release because it's very volatile and because it doesn't change anything for the Fed. Moreover, there's a positive correlation with the US Manufacturing PMI which releases much earlier.

title: US tariff details are better than the worst-case scenario implied yesterday
body: The US is taking another step towards rebuilding the tariff regime that was struck down by the Supreme Court in February. Yesterday's WSJ report highlighted the potential for broad new tariffs but the details from senior US officials in a Reuters report just out are somewhat better than feared. Proposed 20% tariff on China, consistent with the existing trade agreement New tariffs won't stack on top of the 10% and 12.5% forced-labor tariffs Tariffs capped at 15% for South Korea, Taiwan, EU, Japan, Switzerland Capped at 18% for Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Bangladesh Capped at 20% for China Implementation in January at the earliest Final tariffs will be consistent with existing trade deals More targeted tariffs on countries other than China No new tariffs proposed on Mexico or Norway US officials don't anticipate Chinese retaliation Brazil faces additional tariffs under a separate Section 301 investigation, including a proposed 10% tariff on finished aircraft. The biggest detail here is that the tariffs won't stack. That's effectively a 7.5 percentage point increase for China on goods currently subject to the 12.5% levy, something that was floated as far back as August. Officials said China would warrant a 40% tariff in the absence of a trade agreement. None of this should come as a big surprise.

title: What Are Barriers in Trading? Learn About Defined-Risk Contracts in Our Free Webinar
body: Financial markets can move sharply in response to economic news, political developments and unexpected events. For retail traders, sudden price movements can result in significant losses, particularly when stop-loss orders are affected by market volatility and slippage. Barriers offer an alternative approach to managing trading risk, allowing investors to define their maximum potential loss before opening a position. Available to investors in the EEA, these derivative contracts include predefined barrier and take-profit levels, providing greater certainty over potential losses and trade execution. But how do Barriers work, and what makes them different from traditional leveraged trading? What Are Barriers in Trading? Barriers are derivative contracts that allow traders to set predefined price levels at which their positions automatically close. Traders pay an upfront premium, which represents their maximum potential loss. Unlike traditional margin-based trading, Barriers do not involve margin calls or negative balances under their stated terms. Key features include: Guaranteed stop-loss and take-profit: Positions close at the specified price when either level is reached. Known risk: The upfront premium represents the maximum potential loss. title: Market playbook: Where do investors hide when stocks, gold and Bitcoin are all struggling?
body: When everything seems to be on fire, where does one go to hide? Stocks are struggling, gold isn't offering much shelter and Bitcoin is hardly living up to its billing as digital gold. Even the bond market isn't exactly welcoming as of late, even though we are seeing yields come off the boil in the past week. At this juncture, you'd be forgiven for thinking that stuffing money under the mattress is starting to look like a half-decent investment strategy. Jokes aside though, diversification might sound great on paper. However, what happens when the things you own for entirely different reasons all start moving in the same direction? Now, that's a real problem. Higher bond yields, persistent inflation worries and a scramble for liquidity can create precisely that sort of headache. And when investors need to raise cash or when they are forced to reduce leverage, they don't necessarily sell what they dislike. Sometimes, they simply sell what they can. So, where should one be looking in this sort of market environment? Always remember this. Holding on to cash is a position too. Often times, investors underestimate the value of simply sitting on their hands when it comes to trading. The idea of not losing money i.e. capital preservation can at times be a better one than bleeding your account balance dry. title: Why a forex prop firm's headline numbers leave part of the story untold
body: You can get a currency trade right and still have a different result from the one the offer's headline suggests. A profit on the platform is one figure. The amount you can request, when you can request it and what you paid to reach that point are separate questions. That gap matters before you choose an evaluation. A large account balance can sit beside a much smaller loss allowance, while a high profit split may apply to only part of the profit shown. The entry fee does not tell you what another attempt would cost. When you compare a forex prop firm with another, the useful question is what would happen to the same trading result under each offer. A grade can help organize that comparison, provided you can see its criteria, date and which account it covers. The balance is not your loss budget Start with what the account actually represents. An evaluation can measure your trades in a simulation, and passing it does not by itself establish that the next account trades real capital. The word funded needs an explanation of the arrangement behind it. Then separate the starting balance from the amount the account allows you to lose. Leverage determines the exposure you can open, but it does not increase the permitted loss. Check the leverage available on the evaluation account and any lot-size or combined-exposure caps. The calculation matters as much as the allowance. A fixed loss floor stays in place; a trailing floor can rise with performance.

title: Why tight stop losses are just a psychological trap
body: One of the most common mistakes among retail traders is placing stop losses too close to their entry price in an attempt to improve their risk-to-reward ratio. This is basically a psychological trap. A tighter stop loss does not automatically make a trade better or reduce the actual risk. More often than not, it simply increases the probability of being stopped out prematurely by normal market volatility. Let's say you enter a trade with a profit target 100 pips away. By placing the stop loss 20 pips away instead of 50, the theoretical risk-to-reward ratio improves from 2:1 to 5:1. On paper, the second trade looks more attractive. The problem is that the tighter stop also leaves less room for normal price fluctuations. Markets rarely move in a straight line. Even when the underlying trading idea is correct, prices can temporarily move against a position before eventually heading in the expected direction. If the stop loss is too close, normal market noise can trigger it. You might eventually end up taking a loss despite the original idea remaining valid. This can create frustration when the market subsequently moves in the expected direction. You should also keep in mind that we can only control the risk, not the reward. The price might never reach the profit target because market conditions may change. The stop loss should always be placed at the level where the original trading idea becomes invalidated.

The toll from the geopolitical crisis in the Middle East is still being exerted and the impact is still making its way across the European economy in general. Looking at the details, consumer spending showed slight growth (+0.1%) on the quarter while equipment investment is significantly down (-3.5%). Private consumption, which accounts for about 70% of total consumption expenditure, rose by 0.1%. Meanwhile, gross fixed capital formation fell by 1.2% on the quarter. Besides that, the trade mix also changed compared to what we saw in the first half of the year. Exports fell by 1.0% on the quarter while imports fell by 1.4% on the quarter. The breakdown notably shows a sharp fall in service exports (-1.7%) but there were also declines in exports of motor vehicles and motor vehicle parts, chemical products, and metals. Overall, this points to some moderation in growth conditions in Europe's largest economy in Q3 after a decent showing in Q1 and Q2 despite the challenges from the US-Iran conflict. The preliminary hard data for Q4 suggests that things should continue to hold up as well to round off the year, so that will at least afford the ECB some breathing room in their battle against inflation.

title: Beige Book: Eight of 12 districts report growth as wage pressures pick up
body: Eight districts reported growth in the slight to moderate range, and four reported no change. In October, nine grew and three were unchanged. Consumer spending was little changed as households remained price sensitive and selective. Employment rose slightly on balance, with hiring mostly to replace attrition. Wages and benefits rose moderately, up from modest in the prior report. Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior period. Input cost growth generally outpaced increases in selling prices. Most districts expect slight to moderate growth. The November Beige Book shows an economy grinding sideways rather than deteriorating further, but the inflation story has shifted from prices to wages. Boston slipped to no change from slight growth, joining Chicago, Kansas City and San Francisco in the flat column. Dallas slowed to modest from moderate. Cleveland was the lone upgrade, to moderate growth, on robust manufacturing demand tied to data centers, power generation and defense. Construction declined amid higher borrowing and building costs, and residential real estate weakened. Wages are the most important change. Wages and benefits rose moderately after modest gains in October, with pressure concentrated in hard-to-fill roles and driven by cost-of-living demands and rising benefit costs. title: What is order flow trading? How to read buying and selling pressure beyond chart patterns
body: Why good chart patterns fail: What traders should know about market context and order flow Heavy selling does not always mean prices are about to fall. Understanding how the market responds to buying and selling can help traders become more selective about their entries. You learn a chart pattern, recognise it on your screen and enter a trade. A few minutes later, the market moves against you. You followed the textbook, so what went wrong? Perhaps the pattern itself wasn't the problem. It was the market environment in which you decided to trade it. In his Bookmap webinar, Understanding Market Context and Order Flow with Bruce, trader Bruce explains why understanding the bigger picture and observing the behaviour of buyers and sellers can be so valuable. Understanding Market Context and Order Flow with Bruce. Source: Bookmap. Watch on YouTube. Think of the market as an auction Every completed trade involves a buyer and a seller. Yet some participants are more eager to trade than others. Imagine a stock trading around $100. Some buyers are happy to place limit orders at $99 and wait. Others want to buy immediately and are willing to accept the available selling price. The first group provides liquidity by placing resting orders. The second takes liquidity by trading against available sell orders. In order flow terminology, we refer to these as passive and aggressive participants. title: October new home sales 701k vs 650k
body: Prior was 676K (revised to 614K) The US Census Bureau and the Department of Housing and Urban Development publish the New Residential Sales report monthly at 10 am ET, usually in the last week of the month. It tracks sales of newly built single-family homes and is reported as a seasonally adjusted annualized rate. Unlike existing home sales, which count closings, new home sales are recorded when a contract is signed or a deposit is accepted. That makes the report a more timely gauge of housing demand, reflecting buyers' decisions in the reference month rather than one or two months earlier. New homes account for only about 10% to 15% of total home sales, but they matter more for the economy because each one drives construction activity, hiring and spending on materials and furnishings. The data are notoriously volatile. Margins of error are wide, and monthly changes are often not statistically significant. Revisions to the prior three months can be large enough to reverse the initial signal, so economists lean on three-month averages and longer trends. The report also includes the median and average sales price of new homes, inventory of homes for sale and months' supply at the current sales pace. Inventory is broken down by homes not yet started, under construction and completed. A rising stock of completed, unsold homes is a warning sign for builders, since those are the homes they're most eager to move. Results are split by region: Northeast, Midwest, South and West.

title: Gold futures drop below $3,500 as October core PCE hits 3.3%.
body: Gold futures dropped more than 3.2% to $3,475 an ounce, falling below the $3,500 level as a firmer U.S. dollar and an equity sell-off pressured precious metals. October core PCE came in at 3.3% year over year, the highest reading since 2023. Following the inflation print, markets priced in a 94.6% probability of a 25 bps interest rate hike at the Dec. 9 FOMC meeting, lifting the implied rate to 4.11%. Looking ahead, market pricing reflects expectations for additional rate hikes at the January and March meetings, with the implied rate peaking near 4.5% by mid-2027. Traders also monitored potential U.S. tariff announcements on goods from China and the European Union. Across the broader metals complex, Mar Silver futures fell more than 5.5% to $38.93, sliding below $40, while Mar Copper futures declined 2% to $5.34 amid weakness in technology shares and uncertainty around artificial intelligence capital spending.

title: Core PCE heats up as Q3 GDP climbs to 4.3%.
body: Bob Iaccino covers a broad market pullback as Nasdaq futures drop 3.25% and new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners enter the spotlight. Treasury yields ease as the 5-Year falls six basis points and the 10-Year drops seven basis points, while the USD climbs against the euro, yen and pound. October headline PCE rises 0.3% on the month, while core PCE reaches 3.3% year over year and third-quarter GDP is revised up to 4.3%. Plus, traders await the Fed's Beige Book, a $44 billion 7-Year Treasury Note auction, German Consumer Climate and Tokyo Core CPI ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday closure.

title: Swiss Franc futures rally as U.S. core PCE hits 3.3%.
body: Swiss Franc futures advanced for the third time in four sessions, climbing roughly 0.7% after trading between a low of 119.73 and a high of 120.97. Safe-haven currencies, including the Swiss franc, Japanese yen and U.S. dollar, outperformed overnight as a U.S. technology sell-off and concerns over artificial intelligence spending and tariffs weighed on risk sentiment. Upward momentum in the franc continued after U.S. core PCE inflation came in hotter than expected at 3.3% year over year, putting additional pressure on equities after the open. In Switzerland, October inflation reached a three-year high, leading market participants to price in two Swiss National Bank rate hikes by September while anticipating a hold at the December policy meeting. Traders are now monitoring Monday's upcoming Swiss inflation release for further direction on rate expectations.

title: 10-Year T-Note futures climb as yields hit lowest since September.
body: 10-Year T-Note futures advanced as the 10-Year Treasury yield declined 7 bps to close near 4.85% ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. During an early risk-off session, the 10-Year yield dropped to an intraday low of 4.80%, marking its lowest level since Sept. 9. While equity markets staged a late recovery, yields remained near session lows. Meanwhile, the yield curve flattened further, with the spread between the 2-Year and 10-Year Treasury yields narrowing to 20 bps and approaching year-to-date lows. Market expectations continue to point toward rate hikes in December and March, though the path further out on the calendar remains uncertain. Treasury CVOL spiked during the morning move before pulling back from session highs as equities rebounded. Looking ahead, market participants await Friday's trade balance and wholesale and retail inventory reports, followed by next week's employment data culminating in nonfarm payrolls.

title: WTI Crude Oil futures top $83 as EIA reports inventory build.
body: WTI Crude Oil futures climbed over 1.2% to trade back above $83 per barrel as ongoing Middle East tensions and low global inventories outweighed a weekly domestic supply build. The latest EIA report for the week of Nov. 20 showed gasoline stocks rising by 1.7 million barrels and distillate inventories increasing by 700,000 barrels. Refinery utilization rose 1.8% alongside a 33,000-barrel-per-day increase in domestic production. Regional inventories diverged as Cushing crude stocks drew down by 600,000 barrels while PADD 3 inventories built by 1.5 million barrels. In the natural gas market, Jan Natural Gas futures edged higher to $3.66 while the expiring Dec contract fell 1.6%. Market participants are monitoring warmer U.S. temperature forecasts from Nov. 30 through Dec. 4 and awaiting the upcoming EIA storage report, where consensus projects a 24 Bcf withdrawal matching the five-year average.

title: Soybean and Corn futures climb ahead of holiday as Wheat mixed.
body: Soybean and Corn futures advanced in pre-holiday trading, while Wheat futures finished mixed after rebounding from early session lows. Jan Soybean futures traded within a 26-cent range, rising 12.5 cents at one point to 1247'2, while Mar reached 1247'6 alongside a $42 monthly gain in Soybean Meal futures and continued export interest from China. Soybean CVOL stood at 14.5%, compared with 26% for soybean oil and 23% for meal. Corn futures gained on short covering ahead of the holiday despite mixed demand forecasts and favorable weather in South America. The Dec contract reached 440'6 as options traders migrated positions out of December, adding 3,200 calls and 1,200 puts to bring total call open interest to 372,000 contracts. Corn CVOL registered 16%. Wheat futures recovered from an early 11.75-cent decline amid large global supplies. Chicago Wheat futures traded across a 13.5-cent range to reach 591'0, with the Dec contract touching 571'0 and Kansas City Wheat futures reaching 634'4.

title: Live Cattle futures fall on pre-holiday profit-taking.
body: Live Cattle, Feeder Cattle and Lean Hog futures all finished lower ahead of the holiday. In the beef complex, year-over-year supply increases prompted traders to take profits after a recent run-up. Feb Live Cattle futures dropped $3.07 to $226.75, while Apr moved down to $229.12 and Dec reached $223.45, with Live Cattle CVOL at 15.5%. The pullback extended to Feeder Cattle futures, erasing nearly all of the prior week's gains and testing the bottom of the recent trading channel. Jan Feeder Cattle futures fell $6.48 to $326.42 and Mar declined to $322.80, with Feeder Cattle CVOL at 17.4%. Meanwhile, Lean Hog futures gapped down to a new contract low as elevated cold storage supplies and sluggish demand weighed on prices. Feb Lean Hog futures slid $1.50 to $54.92, Apr fell to $63.22 and Dec dropped to $50.07, approaching the $50 level as Lean Hog CVOL reached 34%.

title: E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures slide as Core PCE tops estimates.
body: E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures retreated ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, closing lower in seven of the last nine sessions while volume remained above the 20-day average. Intraday prices ranged from a high of 26,350.75 to a low of 25,027.50, trading down roughly 2.86% late in the session. Semiconductor shares led the pullback, with Nvidia, Micron and AMD weighing on the index as investors evaluated artificial intelligence infrastructure spending and a BNP Paribas downgrade of Micron tied to oversupply concerns. On the macroeconomic front, October Core PCE rose 3.3% year over year compared with expectations of 3.2%, while headline PCE reached 3.8%. Combined with an upward revision to third-quarter GDP at 4.3% annualized and jobless claims of 189,000, the data lifted the probability of a 25 bps rate hike on Dec. 9 to 93.8% according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
